learn.title: Same shape, different size
learn.body: Two figures are similar if one is an enlarged or reduced copy of the other. A photo and its poster are similar. Similar is weaker than congruent: the shape matches, but the size may not.

learn.title: What similar means
learn.body: Similar figures have equal matching angles and matching sides in the same ratio. That ratio is the scale factor $k$. If a small triangle has sides $3,4,5$ and a larger one has sides $6,8,10$, then $k=2$.

learn.title: Perimeter and area
learn.body: Lengths grow by $k$, so the perimeter grows by $k$ too. Area is length times length, so area grows by $k^2$. Doubling every side makes the perimeter twice as big, but the area four times as big.

learn.title: Find a missing side
learn.body: Triangles $ABC$ and $DEF$ are similar. Sides $AB=6$ and $AC=9$. Sides $DE=8$ and $DF$ is unknown.
Write the ratio the same way on both sides: always new over old, or always old over new. Mixing them is the usual mistake.

questions.prompt: A $4\times6$ rectangle is similar to a $10\times15$ rectangle. What is the scale factor from the small to the large one?
questions.explanation: $10\div4=2.5$ and $15\div6=2.5$. Both ratios agree, so they are similar.

questions.prompt: Two similar triangles have scale factor 3. How does the perimeter of the larger compare to the smaller?
questions.explanation: All lengths, including the perimeter, scale by $k=3$.

questions.prompt: Two similar triangles have scale factor 3. The smaller has area 6. What is the area of the larger?
Which statement is true of similar figures?
questions.explanation: Similar figures have equal angles and proportional sides. Sides are equal only when $k=1$.

questions.prompt: Areas of similar figures differ by the scale factor \_\_.
questions.explanation: Area measures two dimensions, so the factor is $k^2$.

questions.prompt: Similar triangles: sides 6 and 9 in the first match sides 8 and $x$ in the second. Find $x$.
A $3,4,5$ triangle is enlarged with scale factor 2. What is the new perimeter?
